title: Choose Voidstation's visual world
question: The roll dealt Projection Booth. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Emerald and the V/ logo stay in every option.

options.label: Projection Booth
options.lineage: 35mm projection booths: changeover cue marks, reel-can labels, Academy leader, the booth log
options.thesis: The Server is the projector and you're the projectionist: it keeps running while you watch the lamp, and nothing changes over without your cue.
materials: sprocket rhythm as the time axis
options.viewport: Assistant: slim booth rail (logo, lamp-status Server strip, conversations as numbered reel cans). The log fills the center: your cues as short lines, answers as full-width reading text, tool checks folded into one sprocket-ticked 'checked' line. The composer is a docked slate with the model stamped on it. Mobile: top bar with lamp, reels in a drawer, slate pinned to the thumb.
options.risk: Cinema props can turn into costume. Every film motif has to do a job (time axis, approval cue, labels) or it's cut.

raised.raise: The course never edits the terrain: Assistant proposals render as their own layer, never mixed into Server readings.
Test strip before commit: every Server control previews exactly what will change before Approve goes live.
Palette law: emerald = running/live, amber = cued/pending/stale, red = fault. No decoration borrows them.
Instrument digits: every measurement sits in a tabular numeral face on its own axis, and the words stay quiet.
Named stages: each Assistant turn moves asked → checking → answered in one fixed place, not a stack of boxes.

options.label: Braun Device Panel
options.lineage: Dieter Rams' Braun appliances: T3, SK4, ET66
options.thesis: Voidstation as a well-made appliance: few controls, perfect engraved legends, and one green key that means go.
options.viewport: Assistant on a quiet panel. The Server gauges sit in a dot-grid strip across the top. Conversation reads like a printout, and the composer is one field with a single emerald key.
options.risk: Familiar: the Rams tribute is where many 'tasteful tool' redesigns land, and it can read as homage rather than your Server.

options.label: Factory Catalog
options.lineage: Peter Saville's Factory Records sleeves: FAC numbers and the Unknown Pleasures pulse plot
options.thesis: Every conversation, reading, and control gets a catalog number, and CPU history becomes a stacked pulse plot in white hairlines.
options.viewport: Black field. The CPU ridgeline owns the top of the Dashboard, and threads are indexed VS-001, VS-002… as a strict catalog.
options.case: Homelab people know this cover by heart, and the ridgeline is a better CPU history. It loses on clarity because coded strips replace words you need on a phone.
options.risk: If the codes aren't translated into plain labels, it becomes a puzzle at 2am when the Server is down.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight
options.thesis: Work moves through fixed stations, and past marked points it's irreversible.
options.viewport: Stations laid out in order, with a test strip before every print.
options.case: Amber wash fights the emerald commitment, and darkroom work isn't the owner's world.
options.kept: Test strip before commit: controls preview exact changes before Approve.
options.risk: An amber monotone drowns state colour.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: Fixed terrain below, and one purple course riding above it.
options.viewport: Server as terrain with Assistant legs drawn over it.
options.case: Clever read-only metaphor, but you don't live in this map, and chat reads poorly as a course.
options.kept: The course never edits the terrain: proposals stay a separate layer from readings.

options.label: CRT Arcade
options.thesis: Fat pixels and phosphor, with palette laws for power and damage.
options.viewport: Server stats as a score bar over a tile playfield.
options.case: Novelty over trust, and pixel type is hostile to long Assistant answers.
options.kept: Palette law: state colours are reserved and never decorative.

options.label: Mesophotic Dive
options.lineage: technical dive computers and depth profiles
options.thesis: One vertical depth axis rules everything.
options.viewport: A dive profile with observations pinned at depth.
options.case: Beautiful, but the ocean says nothing about a home Server or its media.
options.kept: Instrument digits: measurements in tabular numerals on their own axis.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.thesis: One pull turns a flat plane into shaped volume.
options.viewport: A flat surface that gathers into detail on one pull.
options.case: No connection to the owner's world, and clarity suffers.
options.kept: Named stages: each turn moves through a few named states in one place.
options.risk: Fashion costume on a server tool.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished dark app in the Linear/Vercel mould with a ChatGPT-style Assistant, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar with nav and history, a centered chat column, and a floating rounded composer.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other self-hosted dashboard, by design.
